batch_notes: (1) The rubric puts 'exact arithmetic with bignums' under model-oracle while 'the language's stdlib' is external-oracle; decimal and go-humanize lean on math/big in the test, so they are classified model-oracle by the explicit bignum clause, while strconv and math in the same targets are external-oracle. The split is by rubric wording rather than principle and moves ~7 properties. (2) Two targets (decimal, go-ini) express every known bug as a narrowed Hegel property (10 and 7 of them, all pin-tagged, all with direct bug attribution) instead of example pins; the other six targets use example pins, so bug counts per property are not comparable across the batch without the pin split. (3) Several 'RoundTrips'-named properties have the inverse performed in the test rather than by the library (doublestar SplitPattern, glob QuoteMeta): classified spec-postcondition. (4) Several properties are a switch over unrelated checks with different oracles (humanize Ftoa/SI/Ordinal, go-ini KeyHelpers, decimal Constructors): one primary category is lossy there; tags carry the extra oracles. (5) cellbuf's Screen property uses a terminal emulator from the same monorepo (separate module) as oracle; treated as external. Six cellbuf rendering bugs (11-15, 17) are attributed to that single property by inference. (6) Extraction quality: cellbuf property records have empty comment and readme fields (the README documents properties in a table the extractor did not pick up); every decimal property carries the same README list sentence as its readme field. (7) cron's rejection property plausibly produced three of five bugs, but nothing in the batch cites it, so all are inferred.
